title: How to use student advising software tools on Mac for better academic support
metaTitle: Student Advising Software Tools on Mac: A Guide for Academic Advisors
description: Improve your workflow as an academic advisor with student advising software tools on your Mac. Learn how to manage high caseloads and reduce administrative time.
intro: As an academic advisor, your day is often split between meaningful student coaching and repetitive administrative tasks. You can optimize your workflow by integrating your student advising software tools with your Mac environment to save time and focus on your students. This guide explores how to handle high-volume caseloads using your existing tech stack.
tldr: Academic advisors spend 59 percent of their time on non-client administrative tasks.
The average advising caseload is roughly 300 students, leaving limited time for deep coaching.
Advisors want to spend 50 percent less time on transactional tasks like scheduling.
Lazur helps you navigate complex software interfaces and automate repetitive documentation on your Mac.
You can use voice commands to dictate notes, find information, and manage your daily calendar.

blocks.text: The administrative burden of academic advising

Your day as an academic advisor is often defined by the tools you use to track student progress. You likely spend hours in systems like Degree Works or Watermark. These platforms are essential for compliance, but they often require multiple clicks to perform simple actions. You might feel like a data entry clerk rather than a coach. The goal is to move beyond the transactional nature of these tasks. By using your Mac more effectively, you can reduce the time spent on manual input.
Optimizing your Mac for student record management

Most advisors use a mix of institutional software and personal productivity apps. If you use Notion or Obsidian to track student interactions, you can use your Mac to bridge the gap between these tools and your official student information system. Hold the fn key to dictate detailed notes directly into your browser or app. This prevents the need to switch windows constantly. When you are deep into a research session about a student's degree audit, keep your focus on the screen. Use your Mac keyboard shortcuts to manage your windows efficiently. Press ⌘ + Tab to switch between your email client and your student information system.
When handling sensitive student data, ensure you follow your institution's specific policies regarding data privacy and storage. Do not store PII in non-approved cloud services.

blocks.text: Faster with Lazur: Automating your advising workflow

Lazur acts as a bridge between your intent and your Mac interface. When you are stuck in a complex menu structure, you can ask Lazur to guide you. For example, if you need to find a specific report in a dense web portal, ask Lazur to point it out. It will draw a circle around the correct button, saving you from scanning the screen for minutes. This is particularly useful for internal portals that have not been updated in years.
Handling high caseloads with efficient communication

With 300 students on your list, your inbox is likely overflowing. You probably send the same emails about registration deadlines or policy changes repeatedly. Use text expansion tools or built-in Mac features to create templates. When you need to draft a personalized response, hold the fn key to dictate your thoughts. This is faster than typing and allows you to maintain a conversational tone while you work. If you need to search for a specific policy document, use your browser's search function combined with Lazur to summarize the results. This saves you from reading through long PDF files manually.
Common mistakes in student advising workflows

items: Keeping too many tabs open in Chrome, which leads to confusion and slow performance.
Manually copying and pasting student data between systems, which increases the risk of errors.
Failing to use keyboard shortcuts, which adds up to hours of wasted time over a semester.
Not utilizing built-in macOS features like Split View for comparing two student records side by side.
Relying on memory instead of documenting interactions immediately after a meeting.

blocks.text: How to use your Mac for better meeting preparation

Before a student meeting, you need to gather information from multiple sources. You might have a degree audit in one tab, a transcript in another, and your notes in a third. Use the Mission Control feature on your Mac by swiping up with three fingers on your trackpad. This gives you a clear view of all your open windows. Organize your workspace by assigning specific apps to specific desktops. Press ⌃ + Right Arrow to move between these spaces. This keeps your student data organized and prevents you from accidentally sharing the wrong screen during a Zoom call.

If you are a heavy user of PDFs, look into tools that allow for easy annotation. Skim is a popular choice among academics because it lets you export your notes as plain text. This makes it easy to move your findings into your main advising software. When you are reading a long research paper or a policy document, use the built-in text-to-speech feature on your Mac. Go to System Settings > Accessibility > Spoken Content to enable it. This allows you to listen to documents while you perform other simple tasks.

Advising is emotionally demanding. You need to protect your time to avoid burnout. Set clear boundaries on your calendar. Use the Calendar app on your Mac to block out time for deep work or research. Do not let your schedule be entirely controlled by student requests. If you find yourself constantly checking your email, try closing the app for an hour. Use that time to catch up on documentation or plan for your upcoming meetings. Small changes in how you manage your digital space can lead to significant improvements in your daily life.

faq.question: How can I reduce the time spent on data entry?
faq.answer: Use dictation to enter notes quickly and look into text expansion tools to automate repetitive phrases or standard email responses.

faq.question: Is it safe to use AI tools with student records?
faq.answer: You must comply with your institution's data privacy policies. Never upload sensitive student PII or confidential records to unauthorized third-party AI platforms.

faq.question: What is the best way to manage a large student caseload?
faq.answer: Organize your workflow by standardizing your documentation process and using your Mac's workspace features to keep student records separated and accessible.
